findings.title: B2B line refunds have no test, and two refund fixes shipped without one
findings.gap: Line-refund branch unreached by any test
findings.scenario: Refunds are a named critical flow; line refunds are most B2B refunds
findings.blast_radius: 1 file in api/refunds/; every B2B line refund
findings.trace: 1. b2b.py:61 splits whole-order and line refunds. 2. tests/test_refunds.py:12 refunds a whole retail order only. 3. Fixes a1b2c3d and d4e5f6a changed b2b.py:80-97 and no test file
findings.impact: A wrong refund amount reaches customers and the ledger without a test failing
findings.exposure: Critical flow (refunds); fixes a1b2c3d and d4e5f6a changed b2b.py with no test change; 12 commits in the window

coverage.gaps: No test reaches b2b.py; b2b.py:64 constructs PaymentGateway() inline

asserts: A refund of 2 of 5 lines refunds the sum of those lines as rounded today (half-up, b2b.py:97)
The gateway receives exactly one refund call with that amount
A refund above the captured amount raises RefundExceedsCapture and calls no gateway
steps: 1. Pass the gateway into refund_b2b() as a parameter defaulting to PaymentGateway() (verify: tests/test_refunds.py green)
2. Add the line-refund tests with the FakeGateway of F-002 (verify: they fail when b2b.py:97 rounds half-even, green otherwise)
findings.fix: Behaviour tests for B2B line refunds through refund_b2b(), after a gateway seam

validation.evidence: b2b.py:61-104 is imported only by api/routes/refunds.py:30; no test imports either; git show --stat a1b2c3d d4e5f6a lists no test file

findings.title: The shared gateway mock accepts any amount the real gateway refuses
findings.scenario: Every payment and refund test uses this fixture
findings.blast_radius: 9 test files; the checkout and refund flows
findings.trace: 1. conftest.py:30 returns MagicMock() for the gateway. 2. Fix e7f8a9b rounded amounts after the real gateway refused three decimals in production. 3. No test would have failed before e7f8a9b
findings.impact: Any amount or currency the real gateway refuses passes every test
findings.exposure: Checkout and refunds are critical flows; fix e7f8a9b was found in production, not by a test

coverage.gaps: The mock returns success for any amount and currency

asserts: FakeGateway refuses an amount with more than two decimals, as the real API does
FakeGateway records each call so tests assert the amount and currency sent
steps: 1. Add FakeGateway beside the mock in tests/conftest.py (verify: tests/test_payments.py green)
2. Move the payment tests to FakeGateway one file at a time (verify: each file green; test_rounding fails with e7f8a9b reverted on a scratch copy)
findings.fix: A fake gateway that enforces the amount rules, used by every payment test

validation.evidence: tests/conftest.py:30 returns MagicMock(); e7f8a9b's message names the gateway's 400 on three decimals

findings.title: Order placement tests assert only the status code
findings.gap: Weak assertions on a critical flow
findings.scenario: Checkout is a named critical flow; place() changed in 22 commits in the window
findings.trace: 1. tests/test_orders.py:40 posts an order and asserts 201. 2. :118 does the same for a discounted order. 3. Neither reads the total or the stored row
findings.impact: A wrong total or a missing outbox row passes both tests
findings.exposure: Checkout is a critical flow; api/orders/service.py: 22 commits in the window

coverage.gaps: Totals, the persisted order and the outbox row are not asserted

asserts: The response total equals the sum of line prices minus the discount
One order row and one outbox row are stored with that total
steps: 1. Assert the total and the stored rows in both tests (verify: tests/test_orders.py green; fails when service.py:190 drops the discount)
findings.fix: Assert the total, the order row and the outbox row

findings.title: Export worker builds its HTTP client at import, so no test can pass its own
findings.gap: Module-level client with no constructor seam
findings.scenario: Every export test has to patch export.client, because nothing else can reach the client
findings.trace: 1. worker/export.py:22 creates the client at import. 2. Exporter.__init__ takes no client, against ADR 0007
findings.impact: Tests of the export worker can only patch a module global (F-005)
findings.exposure: worker/export.py: 2 commits in the window (below the hotspot bar)

coverage.gaps: The client is created at import (export.py:22); no constructor takes it

steps: 1. Move client construction into Exporter.__init__ as a parameter defaulting to today's HttpClient(), callers unchanged (verify: worker tests green, tests/test_export.py unchanged)
findings.fix: Inject the client as ADR 0007 says, with today's client as the default; coding-refactor work

validation.evidence: worker/export.py:22 client = HttpClient(); docs/adr/0007-worker-wiring.md:9 requires constructor injection

findings.title: Export tests patch a module global and leak it to later tests
findings.gap: Patched module global shared across tests
findings.scenario: tests/test_export.py patches export.client and does not restore it
findings.blast_radius: 1 test file; every test that runs after it
findings.trace: 1. tests/test_export.py:8 assigns export.client without restoring it. 2. Exporter.run() at worker/export.py:30-58 reads that global
findings.impact: Tests after test_export.py see the patched client; results depend on order
steps: 1. Pass a fake client to Exporter in tests/test_export.py and drop the patch (verify: tests pass alone and in reverse order)
findings.fix: Construct Exporter with a fake client once F-004 gives it a constructor parameter

validation.evidence: tests/test_export.py:8 sets export.client = FakeClient() at module level; no teardown restores it
